What we found

Good pavers, tired surface

There’s nothing structural to fix, so you don’t need new pavers. A full restore brings back the color and locks them in.

Your full restore

Three steps, done right

Refresh · deep clean

Professional surface cleaning of every paver with no streaks. Old sand, dirt, weeds and debris come out of the joints, and dark spots are treated.

Re-sand · fill the gaps

Once the pavers are fully dry, new polymeric sand goes into every joint, then it’s compacted and set. It hardens to lock the pavers and resist weeds, ants and washout.

Protect · wet-look seal

A wet-look sealer deepens the natural color and helps protect against stains, UV fading and weeds.

Schedule

Starting December 28 — or sooner

Your date is held for December 28. That’s over a month away, though, and we’d love to get you started sooner.

The clean day can come first
The deep clean is its own day, and it can happen before December 28. You don’t need to be home with us all day: just leave the yard and an outdoor spigot open, and we’ll text you when we’re done. If a day opens up for you, just let Roy know.
Then sand & seal
Once the pavers are fully dry, we come back for the sand and sealer, on December 28 or earlier if you have a day open. Rain moves the date. Sand and sealer only go down on dry pavers.
